Falsifiable claim: splitting core/redact.py into ddflow/core/redact/{__init__,engine,log,pattern,profiles}.py with a lazy __getattr__ re-export preserves the exact public API and redaction behavior. Probe (venv python, not pytest): import ddflow.core.redact as R; from ddflow.core.redact import Redactor; identity R.PROFILES is PROFILES, R.Redactor is Redactor; Redactor("upstream", secret_patterns=[]).text("host [REDACTED:ipv4] home [REDACTED:path]").text == "host [REDACTED:ipv4] home [REDACTED:path]". Verdict CONFIRMED: re-exports bind the same objects and redaction output is byte-for-byte the pre-split behavior.

r-small-files: every submodule is <30k chars (runner 18703 max). layering: submodules import only from lower layers (types<-precommit<-shell<-scratch<-runner, main); the lazy __getattr__ re-export avoids the parent<->child cycle ratchet; no mutual module-level edges. tests/test_layering.py governs it.

data.body: takes exactly one id (+ optional --digest). With many pending complete.force / gate.skip.failed_review requests piling up (a dozen+ after the reviewer/unit_tests wall), the operator has to answer each one-by-one. Add a bulk path:  (approve every pending request, each with its digest recorded), and/or accept multiple  pairs on one command line. Keep the read-receipt digest semantics; still refuse for the agent surface ('answering an approval is a person's act').
data.title: approvals approve: accept --all (or multiple id+digest pairs) for bulk approval

data.summary: The residual main-red holding the whole file-split wave: ddflow/services/reprocheck.py runs git via ['git','-C',...] argv (git_argv x4), os.replace, tempfile, subprocess (run_shell) and breaks the import contract, instead of routing through ddflow/infra.git / core.digest / fsio writers like review_keys/export.select were fixed (B2fc7f7fbba). Plus the split-induced deferred_imports baseline drift (services.review.engine + runner). Fix by routing reprocheck through the shared infra, reconciling the ratchet baselines, so 11-22 pre-existing reds clear and the split wave can merge.
